fixes.explanation: Careful, friend, that one flips the verse upside down. Peter says the opposite: these believers already know these things and are "…established in the truth you now have." (2 Peter 1:12) He says he'll remind them "…even though you know them…" (2 Peter 1:12) So the answer is False, and I think a reminder like that is the kind that sticks.

Teaching is a fine thing, friend, but that's not the word in the verse. Peter wants them "…to recall these things at all times." (2 Peter 1:15) First comes remembering, and that's the part he's working hard on. Believe me, I've tried to pass on a recipe I couldn't remember, and all I had was a mustache and a lot of confidence.

Not this time, friend. Peter says plainly, "…we were eyewitnesses of His majesty." (2 Peter 1:16) He sets that against "…cleverly devised fables…" which they did not follow. So the answer is True, not False.

Perfect, baker. The voice says, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." (2 Peter 1:17) Think about who is speaking: God the Father, from the Majestic Glory. It's a Father saying it about His Son, and Peter says "we ourselves heard this voice from heaven" (2 Peter 1:18).

That one sounds like a line about someone preparing the way for another. Here the voice says something else: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." (2 Peter 1:17) The Father is naming Jesus as His Son, not as a messenger.

Good words, friend, and they're about Jesus. John said, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (John 1:29) But that's a man speaking, and the voice from the Majestic Glory says, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." (2 Peter 1:17)

Water in a desert is a great picture, friend, but Peter doesn't use it. His words are "…a lamp shining in a dark place…" (2 Peter 1:19) Picture me stumbling around my bakery with the lights off. I'm not looking for a drink, I'm looking for the light switch, and I'd still hit the mixer on the way.

A calm sea sounds nice, friend, but Peter doesn't go there. He says to keep paying attention "…until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts." (2 Peter 1:19) Lamp, dark, then the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts. That's the picture he gives.

Good thought, friend, but Peter doesn't mention elders here. He says, "…no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation." (2 Peter 1:20) The word is interpretation, and the verse is telling us what prophecy of Scripture does not come from. Elders aren't in the picture, so that choice doesn't fit.
